species.name: Plain conversational register vs. formal/technical prose
species.instruction: Read the comment's sentence structure and vocabulary only (ignore whether its claims are correct). Score 10 if the writing reads like ordinary spoken conversation: short simple sentences, everyday vocabulary, few or no multi-clause legal/technical constructions, no defined terms or outline numbering. Score 0 if the writing is dense formal/technical prose: long multi-clause sentences, specialized vocabulary, defined terms, or outline/section numbering (I., A., 1.). Score in between for a mix of the two registers.
species.rationale: Plainly-worded conversational comments cluster in dense_high_card_low even when their claims are thin, e.g. R04 ('Its important for many consumers who have health issues...') and R30 ('Hello! I sincerely hope that Boutique Air will continue...'), both dense_high_card_low (.857, .567), versus the outline-numbered technical register of comments like R34 and R39. We expect the dense model to reward easy-to-parse conversational cadence independent of whether the underlying claim is substantiated.
species.upstream_parent: surface-only
all_names: Plain conversational register vs. formal/technical prose

species.name: Verbatim or template-matched cross-submission duplication
species.instruction: Judge only from the single comment text (no access to other comments). Score 10 if the comment reads as a pre-written campaign script: a generic call-to-action bullet list introduced by a stock phrase ('The [agency] needs to:'), a form-letter opening/closing that could be dropped unmodified into any similar submission, and no submission-specific facts. Score 0 if the comment is clearly individually composed, referencing specific facts, dates, docket details, or personal circumstances that would not transfer to another submitter's letter.
species.rationale: R08 and R11 are near-verbatim identical letters ('Please protect Americans from harmful food additives... The FDA needs to: ::Prioritize...') submitted under two different names and cities, and R16/R28 share the same 'Ohio's pollution is on the RISE!... enthusiastically support... Air Nuisance Rule' paragraph verbatim. All four score dense_high_card_low (.550-.676), suggesting the dense model treats a fluent template as a fresh, consequential argument each time it appears. Campaign text can still be factually accurate and professionally researched, so this is mixed.
species.upstream_parent: advocacy-organization-run mass comment campaign supplying pre-written text to individual submitters

species.name: Unhedged rhetorical certainty and enthusiasm markers
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment is dominated by unqualified declarative assertions and confidence/enthusiasm markers (e.g. 'clearly', 'obviously', 'common sense', 'enthusiastically support', 'should act quickly', exclamation points) with little acknowledgment of complexity, trade-offs, or uncertainty. Score 0 if the comment consistently hedges claims, poses open questions, or explicitly flags uncertainty or complexity ('it is unclear whether...', 'further study needed', 'may or may not').
species.rationale: R12 ('it would be common sense to keep that away from the public...') and R16/R28 ('I enthusiastically support... should act quickly... the fastest, most direct means') are confident and unhedged, and all score dense_high_card_low (.657-.769) despite offering little evidentiary support. We expect confident phrasing to read as persuasive to an end-to-end reader independent of whether the underlying claim is actually well-supported.
species.upstream_parent: surface-only
all_names: Unhedged rhetorical certainty and enthusiasm markers

species.name: Administrative placeholder content instead of substance
species.instruction: Score 10 if the visible text is primarily a procedural/administrative placeholder -- e.g. a request to extend the comment period, a cover note saying the real comments are attached or forthcoming, or a brief organizational-identity paragraph -- with little or no engagement with the rule's actual content. Score 0 if the visible text substantively engages the rule's provisions, requirements, or effects.
species.rationale: R25 ('GADA... is requesting a 60-day extension... GADA and its members are actively developing comments') and R59 ('the formal letter is attached to this submission as a pdf file, since the comments exceed the character limit for this system') contain almost no engagement with the underlying rules, yet they carry the two highest dense scores in the entire dense_high_card_low half of this slice (.932 and .916). This suggests the dense model rewards confident, clean, letterhead-formatted administrative prose even when it is a placeholder rather than a substantive comment.
species.upstream_parent: comment filed as a procedural placeholder early in the docket lifecycle (extension request, or promise of forthcoming substantive comments), before any completed substantive analysis
all_names: Administrative placeholder content instead of substance

species.name: Submitting-organization scale/prestige self-description
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment spends substantial text describing the scale, prestige, or brand recognition of the SUBMITTING organization itself (member counts, revenue/market-share figures, named brand-name members or partners, employee counts, facility counts) rather than the rule's substance. Score 0 if the comment contains no such self-description, or only a brief one-line identification of the submitter.
species.rationale: R14 lists all 52 BICEP member brands (Adobe, Nike, Patagonia, Starbucks...), R55/NAMIC touts '1,500 local, regional, and national member companies, including seven of the top 10 property/casualty insurers... 55 percent of the auto market', and R46/Advocate Health cites '150,000 team members... 67 hospitals... nearly $5 billion in annual community benefits' -- three of the highest dense scores in the slice (.902, .895, .865). A well-resourced organization plausibly both gets more attention from the dense model and genuinely tends to write better-evidenced comments, so this is mixed.
species.upstream_parent: well-resourced, high-status submitting organization

species.name: Tenure/place-based persona anchoring
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment establishes the writer's persona primarily through stated personal tenure, residency length, or generational/occupational identity tied to a place or trade ('26 year resident of Kodiak', 'lifelong Canton, NY family', 'watermen and women... June through October') used as a credibility device, independent of any data or citation. Score 0 if the comment contains no such tenure or place/occupation-identity framing.
species.rationale: R29 ('I am a 26 year resident of Kodiak, have fished out of Kodiak for 30 years...'), R41 ('We serious watermen and women are on the water daily from June through October...'), and R30 ('We are a lifelong Canton, NY family who travel quite a bit...') all use tenure-based self-identification and all score dense_high_card_low (.854, .835, .567). Long tenure can genuinely reflect real experiential expertise, so this is mixed rather than purely spurious.
species.upstream_parent: submitter's long-standing informal standing within the affected community or industry (long-term resident, multi-generational occupational identity)

species.name: Formal legal case-law citation apparatus
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment cites case law in formal legal citation format (case name, reporter volume/page, court, 'v.', 'See e.g.') or is issued under a law firm's letterhead or 'Counsel to' signature block. Score 0 if the comment contains no case-law citations and no legal-counsel signature block.
species.rationale: R33 cites 'Pud No. 1 v. Washington Dept of Ecology, 511 US 700 (1994)', R21 cites 'Knight Hawk Co., 991 F.3d 1297 (D.C. Cir. 2021)', and R03 is filed under an 'Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld LLP... Counsel to the Small UAV Coalition' signature block -- all three score dense_low_card_high (.050, .287, .094), the lowest end of the whole disagreement slice. Legal-citation apparatus is exactly the kind of thing that should matter for an agency assessing legal soundness, so this factor is mixed even though dense appears to discount it.
species.upstream_parent: comment drafted or reviewed by a law firm or professional lobbyist

species.name: Agency-relationship disclosure
species.instruction: Score 10 when the writer explicitly describes prior permits, recurring meetings, ongoing communications, or previous dealings with the agency; score 0 when no prior agency relationship is mentioned.
species.rationale: R53 emphasizes decades of work with NMFS’s Office of Protected Resources and repeated permit communications; R25 cites a previously approved exemption; R58 describes multiple member meetings and agency coordination. These fingerprints may cue insider status rather than merit.
species.upstream_parent: existing relationships with agency personnel or programs
all_names: Reference to standing institutional relationship with the agency

species.name: Personal anecdote as the sole evidentiary support
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment's entire argument rests on a first-person anecdote or personal experience ('I noticed...', 'in my case...') with no external citation, data, or source referenced anywhere in the text. Score 0 if the argument is built on external sources, data, regulatory text, or reasoning that does not depend on the writer's personal experience.
species.rationale: R22 argues entirely from the writer's own vehicle-camera experience ('I can attest that in vehicles without rear view mirrors, they are extremely helpful...') and R49 argues from personal knowledge of a single bankruptcy case ('Texas cattle producers know firsthand... Sam Kane Beef Processors LLC...') with no external citations in either; both score dense_high_card_low (.826, .652). Genuine frontline experience can be real evidence, so this is mixed rather than purely spurious.
species.upstream_parent: individual layperson submitter without institutional or research resources to marshal external evidence
all_names: Personal anecdote as the sole evidentiary support

species.name: Editorial subheading/document-design polish
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment uses descriptive thematic subheadings or bolded/lettered section titles that summarize the argument to follow (e.g. 'Minimal Economic Benefit', lettered or numbered proposal sections), giving it a professionally laid-out document structure. Score 0 if the comment is unstructured continuous prose with no subheadings.
species.rationale: R14/BICEP uses a bolded subhead ('Minimal Economic Benefit') to organize its argument, and R46/Advocate Health uses lettered section headers ('A. IRF PPS Payment-Related Proposals... B. IRF PPS Quality-Focused Proposals') -- both score dense_high_card_low (.902, .865). Well-organized document design plausibly also reflects genuinely more careful, well-organized argumentation, so this is mixed.
species.upstream_parent: professional editing or institutional communications support in preparing the submission

species.name: Place-anchored lived-tenure standing claim
species.instruction: Score how strongly the writer stakes a claim to firsthand standing by anchoring themselves to a NAMED place plus a COUNTED span of time or a concrete owned asset. 10 = an explicit locality plus a number of years plus a tangible stake, e.g. 'I am a 26 year resident of Kodiak, have fished out of Kodiak for 30 years and own the 85 foot Caravelle', 'wholesaling fresh fruits and vegetables in Philadelphia for over 100 years', 'over 20 years of experience studying the Argentine ant in the field in California'. 5 = a generic affiliation with no place, no tenure, and no asset ('as a farmer', 'as a concerned citizen'). 0 = no first-person standing claim at all; the writer never says who they are relative to the regulated activity. Score only the presence and specificity of the standing claim, not whether the argument that follows is good.
species.rationale: This is a costume, not an argument: the fingerprint is a self-description, and it can be worn by a comment whose reasoning is thin. R02 opens with residence-years, fishing-years and vessel length before making any claim; R51 leads with a century of produce wholesaling and then offers only a bare preference about board seats; R27 front-loads 'Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon Fire victim whose house was completely destroyed'; R50 opens with '20 years of experience studying the Argentine ant'. The tenure number is scorable and would be predictive even if the substantive paragraphs were deleted. Marked mixed because genuinely affected parties do also supply real local facts (R02's stand-down history), so the channel cannot be reported as pure noise.
species.upstream_parent: The submitter is a directly regulated or physically affected party, a category agencies treat as evidentiary 'affected-public' testimony independent of argument quality.

species.name: Salutation to named political principal plus adversarial framing
species.instruction: Score how much the comment personalises the rule onto a named political officeholder. 10 = the salutation names the sitting administrator/secretary/commissioner by name or honorific AND the body frames the rule as that person's political act or an 'attack'/'rollback' (e.g. 'Dear Administrator Wheeler ... I strongly oppose President Donald Trump and EPA Administrator Andrew Wheeler's attack on ...'). 5 = names the official in the salutation only, with neutral technical framing thereafter. 0 = addressed to a docket number, an office, 'To Whom It May Concern', or nobody, with no political personalisation anywhere. Do not reward or penalise the policy position itself.
species.rationale: Knowing the incumbent's name is a property of when and through what mailing-list the comment was written, not of what it establishes. R21 and R16 both open 'Dear Administrator Wheeler' on 2019-2020 EPA dockets and are visibly campaign-routed (forwarded 'From:/To:/Date:/Subject:' headers); R36 addresses 'Dear Michael Regan'; R09 leans on Executive Order 13777 language. The channel therefore tags docket era and campaign origin, which no reasonable account of comment merit should include.
species.upstream_parent: The comment was produced inside an advocacy campaign keyed to a specific administration, and/or comes from a docket vintage in which that named principal was in office.
all_names: Salutation to named political principal plus adversarial framing

species.name: Organisational self-inventory with membership arithmetic
species.instruction: Score the presence of a dedicated 'who we are' block that QUANTIFIES the submitting organisation. 10 = a standalone paragraph giving member counts, market or capacity share, founding year, employee counts, dollar figures, or an enumerated roster of member firms (e.g. '190-member ... approximately 91 percent of the total chlorine production capacity', 'more than 1,500 ... member companies ... 55 percent of the auto market', a printed list of 52 member brands). 5 = a one-line identification ('the national trade association representing X') with no numbers. 0 = no organisational self-description; the comment starts with substance or with a personal identity only. Score the block's presence and numeric density, not the organisation's importance.
species.rationale: The block is pre-written and reused verbatim across every docket the organisation files in, so it carries zero information about this rule. R12 spends its entire cover note on the credential paragraph and defers all substance to an attachment; R14 devotes roughly half its extracted text to an alphabetical roster of member companies before any argument; R32 and R47 both open with membership arithmetic and founding dates. Marked mixed because resourced organisations plausibly also write better-evidenced comments, so this channel confounds capacity with content.
species.upstream_parent: A government-affairs or communications staff maintains a reusable boilerplate credential block, which is a direct readout of the submitter's organisational resources.

species.name: Procedural or timing ask instead of merits position
species.instruction: Score the extent to which the comment's PRINCIPAL request is about the process rather than the content of the rule. 10 = the operative ask is procedural — extend the comment period, delay or postpone action, publish earlier, restart or re-notice, add status-tracking, reopen — and the comment takes little or no substantive position (e.g. a letter whose whole content is 'requests a 60-day extension in order to complete the development of comments'). 5 = a substantive comment that also contains a procedural request. 0 = purely substantive; no request about timing, process, or the docket's own mechanics. Judge only what is being asked for, not how well it is argued.
species.rationale: A timing request contains no analysis of the rule whatsoever, yet it is a recognisable move made only by people who file often. R30 is nothing but a 60-day extension request with a trade-association letterhead; R11 opens by asking to 'extend the comment period until March 1' and to 'postpone action'; R13 asks CBP to commit to publishing revisions 60 days rather than 30 days before effect; R56 asks for an application status tracking notification system. Marked mixed because repeat-player status also produces genuinely informed comments elsewhere in the same filings.
species.upstream_parent: The submitter is a repeat player represented by professional regulatory staff or counsel, who know that procedural relief is cheap for an agency to grant and ask for it as a routine move.
all_names: Procedural or timing ask instead of merits position

species.name: Unexplained fluency in the agency's internal process machinery
species.instruction: Score how casually the comment uses the agency's INTERNAL workflow vocabulary without stopping to explain it. 10 = the writer names internal actors, artefacts and routines as if to a colleague — 'District Manager' deficiency letters and plan-approval exchanges, sideboard limits and review documents, subapplication review cycles, named databases, exemption and docket numbers of prior actions, which office processes which form — and describes how that machinery behaves in practice. 5 = correct but generic references to 'the rule' and 'the agency'. 0 = no evidence the writer knows anything about the agency beyond the fact that comments are being accepted. Score process-insider vocabulary only; do not score technical subject-matter expertise.
species.rationale: Process fluency fingerprints a relationship rather than an argument: it shows the writer has been through the pipeline before, which is a property of the submitter, not of the comment. R48 reasons entirely in terms of which Service's internal screening workflow routes forms where; R34 narrates the District Manager deficiency-letter exchange as lived routine; R02 cites sideboard limits and an internal review document by page and table; R56 describes the subapplication wait as experienced from inside. Marked mixed because insiders also often identify real implementation problems.
species.upstream_parent: An existing working relationship and repeated prior interaction between the submitter and this agency's staff.
all_names: Unexplained fluency in the agency's internal process machinery

species.name: Outside-counsel apparatus: pin cites, captions, counsel byline
species.instruction: Score the presence of law-firm document apparatus, independent of legal soundness. 10 = numbered footnotes carrying pin cites to the Federal Register, U.S.C., C.F.R., Public Laws or reported cases; a litigation-style caption ('IN THE MATTER OF / BEFORE THE ... / In the matter of ... Docket No.'); and a signature block naming a law firm or the phrase 'Counsel to'. 5 = a formal 'Re:' line and inline citations but no footnote apparatus and no counsel byline. 0 = no footnotes, no formal citations, no caption, no counsel. Score the apparatus, not whether the legal argument is correct.
species.rationale: The apparatus is a purchasing decision. R43 carries a full 'BEFORE THE / IN THE MATTER OF' caption and an Akin Gump 'Counsel to the Small UAV Coalition' byline while its substantive content is a short endorsement of someone else's petition; R13 and R40 both run numbered footnotes with Federal Register and statutory pin cites. The same substantive point can be made with or without this furniture, so it separates who drafted from what was said. Marked mixed because counsel-drafted filings do tend to be better organised and better sourced.
species.upstream_parent: The comment was drafted or filed by outside counsel or a professional lobbying shop rather than by the interested party itself.
all_names: Outside-counsel apparatus: pin cites, captions, counsel byline

species.name: Paper-origin scan degradation in the extracted text
species.instruction: Score the density of optical-scan damage in the text. 10 = pervasive artefacts — words fused into single tokens ('idonotsupportcombiningtheA&BandC&D'), letter/digit substitutions ('20l5', 'JetBiue', 'DEPARMENTS', '26)5%'), dropped initial letters in names ('oseph T.'), broken percent and date strings, and stray page furniture mid-sentence. 5 = occasional mis-scanned characters that do not impede reading. 0 = clean, natively digital text with no such artefacts. Score only mechanical corruption; ignore ordinary typos, spelling and grammar errors made by the writer.
species.rationale: Corruption introduced after the writer finished writing cannot be evidence of what the writer knew, yet it is a strong, easily scored textual signal. R02 is heavily fused and digit-substituted throughout, R43's signature block dissolves into 'Gregory ,;- I en Akin G p S auss', R13 renders 'DEPARMENTS' and 'JetBiue', R31 loses the initial letter of its signatory's name. Because it indexes filing channel and vintage, any predictive power it carries is pure provenance leakage.
species.upstream_parent: The submission channel itself: a printed, faxed or scanned paper document, which tracks older dockets and submitters without a clean digital filing workflow.
all_names: Paper-origin scan degradation in the extracted text

species.name: Third-party appendix ballast pasted after the argument
species.instruction: Score how much of the text is imported material that is not the author's own argument. 10 = a large trailing block of third-party content — agency brochures, management guidelines, program descriptions, statutory excerpts, blank comment-form tables, or column-shredded reference pages whose lines interleave into nonsense — appended after or around a comparatively short authored comment. 5 = a short quoted excerpt used to support a point. 0 = every paragraph is the author's own composed argument. Score the proportion and rawness of imported filler, not the quality of the authored part.
species.rationale: The ballast is neither written nor selected as argument, and in the extracted form it is often unreadable, so it can only act as a texture cue. R06 appends a two-column TPWD/USFWS habitat-guidelines brochure that shreds into interleaved half-sentences after a short authored comment; R25 pastes a long National Wildlife Federation corridor-examples catalogue; R24 carries blank 'COMMENT # 1 of 10 / Type of Comment (check one)' form scaffolding and repeated letterhead. None of this is the submitter's reasoning.
species.upstream_parent: An attachment-assembly habit: the submitter bundles supporting literature into the uploaded file, and the docket's text extraction concatenates it into the comment body.
all_names: Third-party appendix ballast pasted after the argument

species.name: Unrepresented enthusiast register: gratitude, personal benefit, callback offer
species.instruction: Score the comment's warmth-and-availability register. 10 = the writer thanks or praises the agency or the regulated product, argues from personal consumption or personal convenience, and volunteers direct contact details in the body for follow-up (e.g. 'Thank you for doing such a great job ... please reach out to me at <phone>'; 'I would like to thank the Agricultural Marketing Service for proposing this rule. I am excited ...'). 5 = a polite closing thank-you with no praise, no personal-benefit framing, and no contact offer. 0 = no gratitude, no praise, no personal-consumption framing; the argument is tied to the rule text or to cited evidence. Score register only; a warm comment may still be substantively empty and must still score high here.
species.rationale: This register is a marker of who wandered into the docket, and it attaches to comments with essentially no analytic content. R44 thanks AMS and calls differently coloured carrots 'exhilarating to consume and produce' while predicting they 'may just change the entire course of the agricultural industry'; R03 praises the airline's 'planes, the staff, pilots, EVERYTHING' and prints a phone number for follow-up; R54 and R45 both argue from the writer's own shopping and driving experience. Gratitude is not evidence.
species.upstream_parent: The submitter is an unrepresented individual reached by a locally or consumer-salient docket rather than through a professional or advocacy network, and writes in ordinary correspondence register.
all_names: Unrepresented enthusiast register: gratitude, personal benefit, callback offer

species.name: Mass-campaign template fingerprint with thin signer block
species.instruction: Score how strongly the body reads as a distributable template rather than an individually composed letter. 10 = imperative agency-directive list scaffolding ('The FDA needs to:' followed by parallel demands), campaign-tool typographic artefacts such as '::' bullets or doubled salutations, forwarded-email routing headers ('From: <person> To: <office>-Docket, Date:, Subject: Docket ID No. ...'), a body that could be sent unchanged by any signer, and a closing consisting only of a personal name plus city and ZIP. 5 = an individually written letter that nonetheless recycles a recognisable advocacy talking-point block. 0 = wholly individual composition, with specifics only this writer could supply. Score template shape, not the position taken.
species.rationale: The slice contains near-duplicate pairs that make the channel directly observable: R07 and R20 carry a byte-identical body with '::' bullets, differing only in the signer name and city/ZIP; R57 and R60 share the same Ohio Air Nuisance Rule block, with R60 merely prefixing a personal preamble. R16 and R21 show the forwarded-header routing of a campaign mailer. Since the text is authored upstream and merely re-signed, any score it earns belongs to the campaign, not to the signer.
species.upstream_parent: The comment arrived through a coordinated mass-comment campaign operated by an advocacy organisation, which controls both the wording and the volume.
all_names: Mass-campaign template fingerprint with thin signer block

species.name: Submission-wrapper residue
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment contains abundant portal/email headers, attachment placeholders, filenames, OCR errors, duplicated cover text, or page artifacts; score 0 when it is clean, direct prose.
species.rationale: R03, R47, and R56 contain email metadata, file references, or submission artifacts that can act as document-recognition cues without adding substantive merit.
species.upstream_parent: surface-only

species.name: Campaign template reuse
species.instruction: Score 10 when wording, headings, demands, or paragraph order closely duplicates another apparent submission; score 0 when the wording is clearly original and individualized.
species.rationale: R21 and R56 are effectively identical apart from the signer; R43 and R59 repeat nearly the same Ohio Air Nuisance Rule language. Repetition can be predictive of model salience while providing no independent evidence of quality.
species.upstream_parent: coordinated mass-comment campaign

species.name: Citation ornamentation
species.instruction: Score 10 when formal citations, docket identifiers, footnotes, quoted authorities, or regulatory references are prominent relative to the accompanying reasoning; score 0 when such authority markers are absent.
species.rationale: R30 and R56 use authoritative quotations or case references in compact arguments, while R43 and R39 foreground dense statutory and docket references; citation form can create an authority halo independent of evidentiary strength.
species.upstream_parent: surface-only

species.name: Organizational Size Boasting
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment explicitly itemizes the submitter's market share, number of employees, or exhaustive lists of affiliated member organizations to establish authority. Score 0 if there is no mention of organizational size, membership metrics, or corporate scale.
species.rationale: R50, R36, and R03 list massive membership numbers or dozens of affiliated organizations. Including these metrics is a clear lobbying fingerprint, which the dense model may discount despite the scorecard rewarding such established coalitions.
species.upstream_parent: Trade association lobbying weight

species.name: Coalition consensus packaging
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment claims to represent many organizations, members, or a consensus process and names them; score 0 when it is clearly an individual submission.
species.rationale: R27 lists 52 businesses; R31 lists more than 20 associations; R58 describes 700 members and multiple consensus meetings. Aggregation can make a comment appear consequential even when the underlying reasoning is not stronger.
species.upstream_parent: coordinated organizational mobilization

species.name: Administrative legal fluency
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses polished rulemaking conventions, precise procedural terminology, structured proposed edits, litigation references, or counsel-style drafting; score 0 when it lacks that professional register.
species.rationale: R14, R33, and R39 show highly formal counsel- or association-style drafting with procedural and legal architecture. That style may affect perceived importance apart from the merits, while professional drafting can also improve technical clarity.
species.upstream_parent: law-firm or professional lobbyist drafting

species.name: Agency-familiarity cues
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment names officials, references prior interactions, thanks the agency for coordination, or describes an established working relationship; score 0 when it contains no such relational cues.
species.rationale: R25 says the author worked closely with the relevant office, R32 mentions agency coordination, and R48 addresses a named EPA contact. These cues can signal insider standing without proving the proposal is sound.
species.upstream_parent: existing relationships with agency personnel

species.name: Role-and-tenure anchoring
species.instruction: Score 10 when the writer foregrounds a job, ownership position, local identity, years of experience, or direct operational role; score 0 when the writer supplies no personal or sectoral positioning.
species.rationale: R06 identifies the writer as a FedEx driver, R18 names a fishing vessel and lived experience, and R26 emphasizes decades of fishing and vessel ownership. Such identity anchors may make a comment feel consequential even when the supporting analysis is limited.
species.upstream_parent: submitter standing and firsthand sector exposure

species.name: Sweeping-stakes language
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses totalizing claims about entire industries, all Americans, existential threats, or dramatic economy-wide consequences without proportionate docket-specific support; score 0 when claims remain narrow and bounded.
species.rationale: R02 predicts that the rule will reshape the entire vape industry and create enormous taxpayer costs, while R11 expands a carrot rule into a major agricultural movement and R28 invokes all Americans. Scale rhetoric can be salient without being reliable evidence.
species.upstream_parent: surface-only

species.name: Lifecycle urgency markers
species.instruction: Score 10 when the text reveals deadline pressure, requests an extension or delay, references a prior approval or correction, or otherwise signals a time-sensitive docket stage; score 0 when it contains no lifecycle or timing cues.
species.rationale: R18 and R31 explicitly request comment-period extensions, while R23 references a previously approved exemption and R32 describes a pending submission and attachment. Timing language can affect perceived importance without bearing on substantive merit.
species.upstream_parent: comment timing within the docket lifecycle

species.name: Regulatory-lawyer fluency
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment precisely maps proposed text to docket provisions, CFR sections, statutory authority, or requested edits; score 0 when it offers only broad approval or opposition.
species.rationale: R16 supplies ten structured textual edits with regulatory guidance references; R22 discusses 30 CFR provisions, the APA, the Appointments Clause, and judicial decisions. This procedural fluency can signal professional influence independently of substantive correctness.
species.upstream_parent: professional regulatory counsel or lobbying resources

species.name: Named expert tenure
species.instruction: Score 10 when an individual foregrounds senior title, licensing, specialized expertise, or many years of direct experience; score 0 when the writer supplies no personal authority credentials.
species.rationale: R18 identifies a 30-year fishing history and ownership of an 85-foot vessel; R53 cites more than 30 years of research and 20 years as a permit holder; R60 claims over 20 years studying Argentine ants. These cues may attract dense-model weight apart from the evidence presented.
species.upstream_parent: submitter seniority and professional standing

species.name: Lived-experience vividness
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses concrete personal, family, occupational, or place-based experiences with vivid sensory or emotional detail; score 0 when it remains entirely abstract and impersonal.
species.rationale: R04 describes a destroyed home and difficult recovery process; R14 uses a detailed homeless Christmas narrative; R43 describes living downwind of Ohio industrial plants. Emotional proximity may predict dense scoring without guaranteeing analytical merit.
species.upstream_parent: direct exposure to the affected problem and local standing

species.name: Implementation-workflow specificity
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies concrete forms, responsible offices, transition steps, testing scenarios, timelines, or documentation requirements; score 0 when it states only a general preference.
species.rationale: R12 asks who trains providers and routes forms across military services; R20 specifies HVAC failure tests, power transitions, and acceptable proof; R46 requests application tracking and review timelines. Operational detail may proxy consequentiality, though it can also contain genuine insight.
species.upstream_parent: operational proximity to regulated implementation

species.name: Authority stacking
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment densely accumulates statutes, cases, executive orders, studies, quoted authorities, or named technical sources without proportionate explanation; score 0 when it contains no external authority references.
species.rationale: R40 stacks SIGAR, DoDI, and scholarly-source references; R45 invokes a Supreme Court decision and statutory language; R48 reproduces executive-order and statutory criteria. Citation accumulation can impress a dense model even when the authorities are only loosely integrated.
species.upstream_parent: professional editing and advocacy research capacity

species.name: Advocacy Boilerplate Density
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment contains multiple lengthy paragraphs that read like generic campaign literature, public relations copy, or verbatim text from an external organization's website without any personalization by the submitter. Score 0 if the comment consists entirely of self-contained, original arguments specific to the submitter.
species.rationale: Comments like R34 and R12 use verbatim text from advocacy campaigns (e.g., listing random national wildlife examples). The dense model scores these low (0.125, 0.474), indicating it might be penalizing pasted boilerplate that lacks authentic individual input, even if the scorecard rates them high.
species.upstream_parent: Coordinated mass-mobilization campaign

species.name: Legalese and Memo Formatting
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment uses rigid legal memo structures, formal legal sign-offs (e.g., 'Counsel to...', 'Respectfully submitted'), heavy use of legal reporters, or dense legalese. Score 0 if the comment is written in plain, conversational prose without legal citations.
species.rationale: R20 and R18 feature heavy footnotes, legalistic phrasing, and rigid formatting typical of law firm submissions. The dense model scores them very low (0.266, 0.109), suggesting it discounts professional legal formatting as a proxy for true substantive merit, while the scorecard rewards it.
species.upstream_parent: Law firm or outside counsel drafting

species.name: Explicit Procedural Delay Request
species.instruction: Score 10 if the primary or explicit purpose of the comment is to request a deadline extension, postponement of action, or a longer comment period. Score 0 if the comment solely addresses the substantive merits of the proposed rule.
species.rationale: R06 and R39 explicitly request extensions to the comment period (60-day extension, extend until March). The dense model scores these very high (0.932, 0.835) even though asking for a delay has no substantive merit regarding the actual rulemaking topic.
species.upstream_parent: Strategic docket pacing by regulated entities

species.name: Idiosyncratic Personal Tangents
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment contains highly personalized philosophical reflections, emotional outbursts, or non-sequitur asides unrelated to the technical specifics of the rule. Score 0 if the comment remains strictly on-topic and emotionally neutral.
species.rationale: R38 rambles about how a carrot rule will start a 'major economic movement' for 'exotic goods', while R42 digresses into the 'atrocious smell' of neighbors getting cancer. The dense model scores these high (0.722, 0.676), likely detecting authentic individual stakes, whereas the scorecard penalizes the lack of professional focus.
species.upstream_parent: Unfiltered individual / non-professional author

species.name: Internal Consensus Reference
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment explicitly references internal organizational meetings, working groups, or consensus-building processes used to draft the comment. Score 0 if the comment presents itself as the sole work of an individual with no mention of an internal drafting process.
species.rationale: R13 mentions holding 'multiple meetings among a broad representation of our membership to ensure their input and consensus'. R50 references drafting coordination across a massive association. Citing internal bureaucratic processes is an organizational tell rather than direct evidence of the comment's substantive quality.
species.upstream_parent: Corporate bureaucracy / committee drafting

species.name: Agency Flattery and Praise
species.instruction: Score 10 if the comment contains unprompted, explicit praise for the agency's staff, mission, or processes (e.g., 'We applaud...', 'organized and effective process'). Score 0 if the tone is purely critical, neutral, or strictly transactional.
species.rationale: R23 praises the 'considerable and valuable expertise' of agency staff, and R09 states 'We applaud the Federal Aviation Administration'. Flattering the agency is a relational fingerprint that the dense model might weight differently than pure merit, heavily penalizing R23 and R09 (0.238, 0.269).
species.upstream_parent: Established agency-submitter relationship

species.name: Form Letter Impersonality
species.instruction: Score 10 if the text is generic and completely lacks first-person operational details, reading like a script anyone could sign without modification. Score 0 if the text includes highly specific, individualized details about the author's unique situation.
species.rationale: R08 and R43 use generic, impersonal language ('I support efforts to reduce barriers...', 'Please protect Americans...'). The dense model scores these higher than the scorecard does (0.559 vs 0.055 for R43), but still low overall, indicating a penalty for impersonal form letters that lack unique operational insight.
species.upstream_parent: Mass mobilization campaign

species.name: Parochial Grandiosity
species.instruction: Score 10 if the submitter exaggerates the impact of a highly local or minor administrative issue to a ridiculous, sweeping degree (e.g., claiming a minor rule will change an entire industry or the course of the economy). Score 0 if the submitter accurately and modestly scopes the impact of the rule.
species.rationale: R38 grandiosely claims a rule on colored carrots will 'change the entire course of the agricultural industry', while R30 claims local warehouse concerns demand overriding federal port limits. This hyperbolic inflation of stakes is a fingerprint of a parochial vested interest, which the dense model scores notably high (0.722, 0.365).
species.upstream_parent: NIMBYism or hyper-local economic stake

species.name: Typographical Error Density
species.instruction: Score 10 if the text contains frequent missing spaces, glaring misspellings, broken punctuation, or bizarre formatting glitches indicating a lack of professional editing. Score 0 if the grammar, spacing, and punctuation are flawless.
species.rationale: R44 has glaring errors like 'idonotsupportcombiningtheA&BandC&D' and '26)5%', while R01 has erratic capitalization ('aND'). The dense model scores these relatively high (0.854, 0.334), suggesting it does not penalize poor editing, treating typos as a sign of authentic, individual grassroots drafting rather than a lack of merit.
species.upstream_parent: Lack of professional editing resources
